title: The Garden at Night 🐌 Calm Bedtime Story with Luna
intro: Hello, little one. I'm Luna, the sleepy owl. Welcome back to Moonbeam Bedtime.
Tonight, we'll say goodnight to the quiet garden at night.
First, let's take a slow, deep breath together. Breathe in, and breathe out.
Get cozy, snuggle in under your blanket, and listen softly.
Are you ready? Let's begin our story.

lines: Here's a little clue: she moves very slowly, and she carries a shell on her back. Who could it be?
This is Snail. Can you whisper snail? Nice and soft.
A snail carries her shell everywhere. It's her own little house.
Snails like to come out at night, when the garden is cool and damp.
Can you move your hand very, very slowly, like a snail? Slow, slow, slow.
What does a snail carry on her back?
Her shell. Her own little house.
Let's say it softly together: Snail.
One more time, very quietly, like a little whisper: Snail.
Snail leaves a shiny, silver trail as she glides through the garden.
Here's a little clue: it has soft, fuzzy wings, and it flutters at night. Who could it be?
This is Moth. Can you whisper moth? Nice and soft.
Most moths flutter around at night, while we're asleep.
Moths have feathery antennae that help them smell sweet flowers.
Can you flutter your hands softly, like little moth wings?
At night, under the moon and stars.
Let's say it softly together: Moth.
One more time, very quietly, like a little whisper: Moth.
Moth flutters slowly past the glowing moon.
Here's a little clue: he's green, he hops, and he says ribbit. Who could it be?
This is Frog. Can you whisper frog? Nice and soft.
Many frogs sing at night, to say hello to each other.
Frogs have long, sticky tongues for catching tiny bugs.
Can you sing a very quiet ribbit? Ribbit, ribbit.
At night. Ribbit, ribbit, in the dark.
Let's say it softly together: Frog.
One more time, very quietly, like a little whisper: Frog.
Frog sits on his lily pad, and his song gets softer and softer.
Here's a little clue: she's red, with little black spots. Who could it be?
This is Ladybug. Can you whisper ladybug? Nice and soft.
Ladybugs have wings hiding under their red, spotty shell.
In winter, lots of ladybugs snuggle together to stay warm.
Can you count her spots with me? One, two, three, four, five, six.
Hiding under her red, spotty shell.
Let's say it softly together: Ladybug.
One more time, very quietly, like a little whisper: Ladybug.
Ladybug tucks in her wings and rests on a soft green leaf.
Here's a little clue: it's pink, it grows in the garden, and it has soft petals. Who could it be?
This is Tulip. Can you whisper tulip? Nice and soft.
Some flowers, like tulips, close their petals at night.
In the morning, when the sun comes up, they open again.
Can you close your hands slowly, like a flower closing its petals?
What do tulips do at night?
They close their petals, like they're going to sleep.
Let's say it softly together: Tulip.
One more time, very quietly, like a little whisper: Tulip.
Tulip folds her petals and sways softly in the breeze.
Goodnight, Tulip. See you in the morning.

recap: Let's remember all of our sleepy friends.
Goodnight, Tulip. See you in the morning.
outro: Goodnight, Snail, Moth, Frog, Ladybug, and Tulip. Now close your eyes, and dream sweet, gentle dreams.
Goodnight, little one. Luna loves you. Sleep tight.
